cards.text: This song comes from the sons of Korah, Levites who stood up and praised the LORD with a very loud voice (2 Chronicles 20:19). LOUD singers? My kind of people, friend. They're talking straight to the LORD, and they start by remembering how He showed favor to His land.

cards.question: The sons of Korah remember the LORD showing favor to His land. What did He do for Jacob, His people?
Next, the sons of Korah remember their people's iniquity. What did the LORD do about it?

answers.text: He kept a record of it

cards.text: And He covered all their sin. Friend, I spent YEARS covered in dust in the back of a drawer, so trust me, this is the GOOD kind of covered.

cards.question: The sons of Korah say the LORD held back only part of His fury.

cards.text: Then the song turns, friend. That was the past. Now the sons of Korah are asking the God of their salvation to restore them.

cards.question: Along with restoring them, what do the sons of Korah ask God to put away?

cards.text: Then come the hard questions, one right after another. You can hear it in every line: how long is this going to last?

cards.question: The sons of Korah ask whether the LORD will be angry with them forever.
The sons of Korah ask the LORD to revive them again, so His people may ___ in Him.

cards.text: Then they keep it short: show us Your loving devotion, O LORD, and grant us Your salvation. Friend, back in that drawer, my whole wish list was ONE word long: LIGHT.
The sons of Korah have just asked the LORD to revive them and show them His loving devotion. Now one singer speaks for himself. And for once, he's not asking for anything.

cards.question: After all that asking, what does the singer say he will do now?

answers.text: Listen to what God will say
Go up to the house of God
Write the prayer on a scroll

cards.text: He's going to LISTEN. Friend, I'm a stamper who talks with his mustache, and that thing has not been quiet one day in its life.

cards.question: The singer is sure God will speak ___ to His people and His saints.
The singer says God will let His people return to folly.
The singer says God's salvation is near to those who fear Him.

cards.text: And it's near so that His glory may dwell in their land. Then the singer starts painting a picture with four of God's good things.

cards.question: In the singer's picture, loving devotion and faithfulness have joined together. And righteousness and peace have ___.

cards.text: Righteousness and peace, KISSED. The dead batteries I shared that drawer with argued for YEARS over who had more charge left, and these two just meet up and kiss.

cards.question: In the singer's picture, faithfulness sprouts from the ___ and righteousness looks down from ___.
The singer says their land will yield its increase. What does he say the LORD will indeed provide?

cards.text: One last picture, friend. The LORD Himself is on the move, and righteousness goes out ahead of Him.

cards.question: In the singer's last picture, why does righteousness go before the LORD?

answers.text: To prepare the way for His steps
To clear the nations from the land
To guard the gates of His city

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'This song comes from… (2 Chronicles 20:19).' / 'LOUD singers?' / 'My kind of people, friend.' / 'They're talking straight to the LORD…'. That is over the limit for the opening card.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences: 'Then the song turns, friend.' / 'That was the past.' / 'Now the sons of Korah are asking…'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says 'You can hear it in every line: how long is this going to last?' That isn't true of every line. Verse 6 asks 'Will You not revive us again', which isn't a how-long question. The card also says the questions come 'one right after another', which reaches past the single verse it cites (Psalm 85:5).

rule.text: Noticing: What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: The setup line 'how long is this going to last?' basically hands over the answer to the next card's true or false statement, 'The sons of Korah ask whether the LORD will be angry with them forever' (card 9).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The first sentence recaps verses 6–7 from stop 1 ('The sons of Korah have just asked the LORD to revive them and show them His loving devotion'). Because of that, the card cites Psalm 85:6-8, which reaches outside this stop's range (Psalm 85:8-13). The card also has 3 sentences.

The joke 'I'm a stamper who talks with his mustache, and that thing has not been quiet one day in its life' doesn't land cleanly. The mustache works as his hands, so it gestures. It doesn't make sound. A mustache that is never 'quiet' needs explaining before it contrasts with listening, so a stranger would likely say 'huh?'

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
